chapter: Chicago, Lee Collins and the road
title: Professor Sherman Cook and the risks of promoting bands in the South
summary: Cook, a flashy promoter who couldn't read, gave Danny a chance to go on the road; Danny describes how tours got stranded when it wasn't payday.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Sure. He used to go with my aunt. He was from Vicksburg, really.
He would come down... He was a jive cat, wasn't he, from... He was kind of (?).
Yeah, that's right. You know, they tried, but they were limited. See, you were limited. You know,
you had to have a bankroll to do things. You'd get bankrupt and you'd get a bad name. Because the weather could knock you out. It was...
Yeah. He was a (?). He had all kinds of vests and walking canes, and he'd drink(?) ...(?)...
And he couldn't read and write. But he would get back up for more.
Yes. And say 'Cool it'; you know, he was cool with it. And he was dedicated for more(?) ...(?)... But the man didn't have the education.

It was limited what you could do, because you could send a band out and get stranded. Like, many times you're playing the South, and you'd leave New Orleans and you'd say you're going to play Vicksburg, Hattiesburg, you're going to play Calverton(?), Alabama, you're going to play Pensacola -- you make a little tour. And you're going to play each night or every other night. And man, you get to the town, and nobody comes to the dance because it ain't payday! People ain't got the money.
